note: FROZEN LABELS for scripts/typesafe-route-replay.ts. Every row is a query this repo already committed to an answer for, in a test, with the file and line that pins it. Nothing was labelled by judgement: a label nobody can point at is a benchmark that moves when the benchmark is inconvenient.
storesServerAndName: `expect` is {server, name}, NOT the qualified name, because qualification depends on this machine's mcp.json toolPrefix (mcp-common/search.ts:qualifyToolName). A fixture that hardcoded `hive_get_run` would fail on a box configured with a different prefix.
pinsIsNotDecoration: `pins` records what the cited test actually asserts. Two rows are pinned only by CONTAINMENT — the test says the tool must appear in the shortlist, not that it must be first. Scoring them as top-1 is therefore a HARDER bar than the repo's own tests set, and the accuracy number below is against the INTENDED tool. Saying so here is the difference between a strict benchmark and an overstated one.
whatIsDeliberatelyAbsent: `booster` -> get_metering_usage (test/toolhints.test.ts:118) is NOT here. It is a real documented probe result, but hive_get_booster_wallet is an equally defensible answer to the bare word `booster`, and an ambiguous label measures the labeller rather than the router. Dropped openly rather than kept and quietly excused when it misses.

queries.why: Benchmark 1. The adapter's coverage gate returns ZERO rows for this two-token query. In the measured hierarchy pilot stage 2 could never reach the tool, because its category was not one stage 1 would pick — the answer was not on the ballot. On the 635-tool corpus the lexical ranker has it at rank 7 of a floor of 8: the structural floor saves this query with one slot to spare.
